config.title: Grid auto-placement

intro.title: Grid auto-placement
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple photo gallery layout where images are automatically arranged into a grid. You will learn how to use CSS Grid's auto-placement feature to position items without explicitly defining their row and column lines. The main technology involved is CSS Grid, specifically properties like `grid-auto-flow` and `grid-auto-rows`. This beginner-friendly lesson will help you create organized, responsive layouts efficiently by letting the browser handle the placement of grid items.
intro.usecase: Grid auto-placement is essential for building responsive product galleries, where items automatically flow into available grid cells without manual positioning. E-commerce sites use this to display varying numbers of products per row across different screen sizes. Dashboard widgets and social media feeds leverage auto-placement to arrange cards or posts efficiently as content loads dynamically. This pattern simplifies creating flexible layouts for image grids, card-based interfaces, and modular content sections that adapt to different content quantities.

objectives: Construct a CSS Grid container with auto-placement enabled
Configure grid items to flow automatically into available cells
Implement grid-auto-flow to control placement direction (row vs column)
Manipulate grid-auto-rows and grid-auto-columns to define implicit track sizes
Apply dense packing to fill gaps in the grid layout
Initialize a grid layout where items automatically position without explicit placement
Control the placement of specific items while allowing others to auto-place

steps.title: Create a CSS file and set up a basic HTML container structure
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS file and add a container class with display: grid to prepare for grid layout.
steps.hint: Start by creating a CSS file and defining a class that uses CSS Grid.
steps.seedCode: /* Create a new CSS file and define a container class with display: grid */
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS file is created with a .container class that has display: grid set.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a .container class with display: grid property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the CSS file, but make sure to include display: grid in the .container class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS file or grid container setup is missing. Please create a CSS file with a .container class using display: grid.

steps.title: Define the grid container with display: grid
steps.instruction: In the existing .container class, add the CSS property display: grid; to enable grid layout.
steps.hint: Add the display property with the value grid inside the .container rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container class will have display: grid; applied, making it a grid container.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added display: grid; inside the .container rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container doesn't have display: grid;. Check that you've added it correctly.

steps.title: Set up explicit grid columns
steps.instruction: Add the grid-template-columns property to the .container class to define three equal-width columns.
steps.hint: Use grid-template-columns with a value that creates three columns of equal width. You can use the repeat() function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container class will have grid-template-columns property defining three equal columns.
successCriteria: The .container class includes grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); or equivalent.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using grid-template-columns to create exactly three columns of equal width.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Check that you've added grid-template-columns to the .container class with three equal columns.

steps.title: Add grid gap for spacing
steps.instruction: Add a `gap` property to the `.container` class to create spacing between grid items.
steps.hint: The `gap` property adds space between grid rows and columns. You can use a single value like `10px` for equal spacing.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid container will have spacing between its items when grid items are added later.
successCriteria: The `.container` class includes a `gap` property with a value like `10px`.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added the `gap` property to the `.container` class.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added the `gap` property to the `.container` class with a valid value like `10px`.

steps.title: Style grid items for visibility
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule for .item elements with background color, padding, and border to make them visually distinct.
steps.hint: Create a new CSS selector for .item and define properties like background-color, padding, and border.
steps.expectedOutcome: Grid items will have visible styling with background color, padding, and borders.
successCriteria: A .item selector is created with background-color, padding, and border properties defined.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styling, but make sure to include background-color, padding, and border properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .item selector or required styling properties are missing. Try adding a .item rule with background-color, padding, and border.

steps.title: Observe default auto-placement behavior
steps.instruction: Add more grid items (at least 6) to your HTML structure so there are more items than the defined grid cells (3 columns).
steps.hint: Add at least three more <div> elements with the class 'item' inside your container to exceed the 3-column layout.
steps.analogousExample:
1
2
3
4
5
6
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid will automatically create new rows to accommodate the extra items, demonstrating the default auto-placement behavior.
successCriteria: There are at least 6 grid items in the HTML, exceeding the 3-column layout defined earlier.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some items, but you need at least 6 total items to clearly observe the auto-placement behavior.
steps.feedbackWrong: Please add at least 6 grid items to your HTML structure to create more items than the 3-column grid can hold.

steps.title: Introduce grid-auto-flow: row
steps.instruction: Add the property grid-auto-flow: row; to the .container class to explicitly set row-based auto-placement.
steps.hint: This property controls the direction in which auto-placed items flow into the grid. The value 'row' is the default behavior, placing items row by row.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .container class now includes grid-auto-flow: row;, which explicitly sets the auto-placement direction to row-based.
successCriteria: The .container class contains the property grid-auto-flow: row;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added grid-auto-flow: row; to the .container class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding grid-auto-flow: row; to the .container class. Please try again.

steps.title: Change to grid-auto-flow: column
steps.instruction: In the .container class, change the grid-auto-flow property from 'row' to 'column' to make items flow across columns instead of rows.
steps.hint: Look for the grid-auto-flow property in your .container class and update its value to 'column'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid-auto-flow property is set to 'column' in the .container class, changing the auto-placement direction.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've changed the grid-auto-flow value to 'column' in the .container class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The grid-auto-flow property should be set to 'column' in the .container class to change the auto-placement direction.

steps.title: Use grid-auto-flow: dense
steps.instruction: Add the value 'dense' to the existing grid-auto-flow property in your .container class to enable dense packing.
steps.hint: The grid-auto-flow property can accept multiple values. Add 'dense' after 'row' to fill empty spaces in the grid.
steps.expectedOutcome: The grid-auto-flow property will be updated to 'row dense', enabling the dense packing algorithm to fill empty grid cells.
successCriteria: The .container class has grid-auto-flow: row dense;
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're adding 'dense' to the existing grid-auto-flow property in the .container class.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to modify the grid-auto-flow property to include 'dense' along with 'row'.

steps.title: Combine grid-auto-flow with explicit item placemen
steps.instruction: Add explicit placement for the first grid item using grid-column and grid-row properties,
steps.hint: Use grid-column: 1 / 3; and grid-row: 1 / 3; to make the first item span two columns and two rows.
steps.expectedOutcome: The first grid item will span two columns and two rows, while the remaining items will be auto-placed around it according to the grid-auto-flow: row setting.
successCriteria: The .item1 selector has grid-column: 1 / 3; and grid-row: 1 / 3; properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both grid-column and grid-row properties to .item1.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding explicit placement properties to the .item1 selector. Use grid-column: 1 / 3; and grid-row: 1 / 3; to make it span two columns and two rows.
